commit.message: Stop the test suite racing its own delivery, and write down the house rules

findings.title: live.js still counts orphans with the filter this comment calls blind
findings.description: The rationale here — that `--append-system-prompt-file` only covers the review pass, so a leak in the fix-verification pass was invisible — applies equally to `extension/test/live.js:167-171`, which still queries on `*append-system-prompt-file*`. That teardown check remains unable to see the exact leak this change was written to catch.
findings.suggestion: Consider updating live.js's teardown query to the same `no-session-persistence` filter, or having it call a shared helper, so both suites agree on what an engine process is.

findings.title: Exits 0 whether the report was delivered, rejected, or never finished
findings.description: `DONE` matches failure outcomes (`Dashboard unreachable`, `rejected the report`, `Reporting failed`, `Review failed`, `— skipping`) as well as success, and the 10-minute timeout simply falls out of the loop. All three paths reach `process.exit(0)`, so a CI step or a shell `&&` chain reads a rejected upload as a successful send.
findings.suggestion: Consider deriving the exit code from whether the log actually shows a delivered report, so a rejection or a timeout is distinguishable from success.

findings.title: Top-level async IIFE has no rejection handler
findings.description: Every throwing call in this script — `execFileSync` on a non-repo, `ext.activate`, `JSON.parse` on a truncated `last-review.json` — rejects the IIFE with nothing attached to it. The sibling harness `live.js:179` ends with `.catch((err) => { console.error(...); process.exit(2); })`; without it the failure surfaces as a bare unhandled-rejection trace and `restore()` never runs, so the `vscode` stub stays installed in the process.
findings.suggestion: Consider mirroring live.js and attaching a catch that reports the error and exits non-zero.

findings.title: The orphan query is duplicated verbatim from engineClaudePids()
findings.description: This block re-declares the same PowerShell script and the same parse pipeline that `engineClaudePids()` (qa.js:114) already contains. The two must stay identical for the baseline subtraction to mean anything — if one filter is later retuned and the other isn't, `preexisting` and `count()` start describing different process sets and the subtraction silently under- or over-counts.
findings.suggestion: Consider calling the existing helper here so there is one definition of what an engine-spawned Claude process looks like.

findings.title: Baseline excludes processes that predate the run, not just other runs' processes
findings.description: The comment reads "Count only processes this run started", but `preexisting` is sampled once at startup, so the filter only excludes processes alive before the suite began. A second suite or a live test that starts *after* the baseline still contributes PIDs that survive `mine()` — the concurrent-run false alarm the comment describes can still occur, just in a narrower window.
findings.suggestion: Consider softening the comment to what the baseline actually guarantees ("ignore processes that predate this run"), so a future reader doesn't trust it to cover concurrent starts.
